name: Abell 85 (Hubble)
blurb: Abell 85, a galaxy cluster, seen by Hubble.
label: abell85-hubble
story: A quiet spot inside the galaxy cluster Abell 85, where a Type Ia supernova once exploded with no galaxy around it. Hubble found nothing at its location, a sign that the star belonged to the faint population of stars stripped from their home galaxies.

claims.text: The target ABELL85-6-08-0 is the location of an apparently hostless, now-faded Type Ia supernova in Abell 85, imaged with deep HST ACS observations
Hubble detected no object at the supernova's location; the SN Ia in Abell 85 is truly hostless
Hostless SNe Ia support the idea that their progenitors belong to the intracluster stellar population
Intracluster light in Abell 85 is the glow of stars stripped from their home galaxies
